title: Match the equation to a table or graph
subtitle: Linear equations in two variables · 24 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **24 of the official questions in Linear equations in two variables are this one** — 9 Easy, 9 Medium, 6 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Easy tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're given a table of x and y values or a graphed line and asked which equation represents the relationship, or you're given an equation and asked which table fits it.
- All four choices are equations (or tables), sometimes with an unknown positive constant.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Take two clear points and find the slope, then the y-intercept (the y-value where x = 0 if the table has it).
- 2) Write y = mx + b, or rearrange to match the choices.
- 3) Faster option: substitute two points into each choice and keep the one that works for both.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the table into a Desmos table, type each choice as an equation, and see which line passes through every point.
For a graph with labelled points, plot those points the same way.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: A choice that passes through one point but not the other, a slope computed as run over rise, or an intercept with the wrong sign.
When a constant k appears, you might treat it as a number instead of reading it from the graph's labelled intercept.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
A choice that passes through one point but not the other, a slope computed as run over rise, or an intercept with the wrong sign.
When a constant k appears, you might treat it as a number instead of reading it from the graph's labelled intercept.
